The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` fails because the method `isUnixSymlink` incorrectly returns true when Unix permissions include multiple flags (such as 177777). From the code of `isUnixSymlink()`, it returns true when `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. The value of `LINK_FLAG` is octal 0120000, indicating the bit flag for a Unix symbolic link.

The method `getUnixMode()` returns the Unix mode bits only if the platform is Unix (constant PLATFORM_UNIX = 3). It extracts the mode by shifting external attributes and masking with a short mask. This means it retrieves the 16-bit Unix permission bits from the external attributes of the Zip entry only for Unix platforms.

The bug occurs because `isUnixSymlink()` only checks if the link bit is set, but does not ensure that no other bits are set. This means if the mode has multiple bits set including the link flag, `isUnixSymlink()` will still return true — which is incorrect. The test proves this by giving an entry that has more than one flag set in the Unix mode (177777) but is not a symlink, yet `isUnixSymlink()` returns true.

Thus, the root cause is that `isUnixSymlink()` only checks for the presence of the link flag bit and doesn't confirm it is the sole or exact file type flag set. Proper detection of symlink should confirm exclusivity or correct permission mask, which is currently missing.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
